unacceptable_risk.description: AI systems considered a clear threat to safety, livelihoods and rights of people
examples: Cognitive behavioural manipulation of people or specific vulnerable groups
Voice-activated toys that encourage dangerous behaviour in children
Social scoring AI classifying people based on behaviour, socio-economic status or personal characteristics
Real-time biometric identification systems in publicly accessible spaces

high_risk.description: AI systems that pose significant risks to health, safety, or fundamental rights
regulatory_requirements: Transparency and provision of information to users
high_risk.classification_criteria: Defined in Article 6 - systems used in areas listed in Annex III

limited_risk.description: AI systems with specific transparency obligations
requirements: Inform users they are interacting with AI system

minimal_risk.description: AI systems with minimal or no risk
minimal_risk.requirements: Voluntary application of codes of conduct

general_purpose_ai_models.definition: AI model that displays significant generality and is capable of competently performing a wide range of distinct tasks

requirements: Draw up and keep up to date technical documentation
Provide information and documentation to downstream providers
Put in place policy to respect Union copyright law
Publish detailed summary of content used for training

threshold.description: Amount of compute used for training measured in floating point operations

additional_obligations: Conduct model evaluation in accordance with standardised protocols
Assess and mitigate possible systemic risks
Track, document and report relevant information about security incidents
Ensure adequate level of cybersecurity protection
Report to Commission on serious incidents

market_designation.description: Commission may designate models below 10^25 FLOPs as systemic risk
market_designation.criteria: High-impact capabilities equivalent to models above threshold

compute_threshold_compliance.description: Models above 10^25 FLOPs are subject to systemic risk obligations

high_risk_deployment.description: High-risk AI systems require comprehensive compliance measures

prohibited_practices.description: AI systems for social scoring or mass surveillance are prohibited

transparency_requirements.description: AI systems interacting with humans must disclose their nature

applicable_provisions: Article 53 - General purpose AI model obligations

key_definitions.ai_system: Machine-based system that is designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy and that may exhibit adaptiveness after deployment, and that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers, from the input it receives, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments
key_definitions.provider: Natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body that develops an AI system or a general-purpose AI model or that has an AI system or a general-purpose AI model developed and places it on the market or puts the AI system into service under its own name or trademark
key_definitions.deployer: Natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body using an AI system under its authority
key_definitions.flops: Floating point operations - unit of measurement for computational work in AI model training

systemic_risk_classification.template: systemic_risk_model(Model) :- model(Model, Org, compute(C), risk_score(R)), C > 1e25.

current_models_analysis.note: As of 2024, approximately 8 models are estimated to meet the 10^25 FLOPs threshold
